senses.gloss: All the people who belong to an organization, taken together.
examples: The union's *membership* voted to accept the contract.
The club surveyed its *membership* about the dues increase.
Our *membership* is mostly retired teachers and nurses.

senses.gloss: A ceremony held to honor someone who has died.
examples: The family is holding a *memorial* on Saturday afternoon.
About two hundred people came to his *memorial*.
She spoke at her coworker's *memorial* last month.

senses.gloss: A thing or event that stands for something larger.
examples: The empty factory became a *metaphor* for the whole town's decline.
For her, the marathon was a *metaphor* for getting better.
Critics read the storm in the film as a *metaphor* for grief.

senses.gloss: A very short radio wave, used to carry signals and to heat food.
examples: The station relays the broadcast by *microwave*.
*Microwaves* heat food by shaking the water in it.
Radar works by bouncing *microwaves* off distant objects.

senses.gloss: The movement of people from one country or region to another to live there.
examples: The war set off the largest *migration* in the region's history.
Economists study the *migration* of workers to the Sun Belt.
*Migration* from the countryside emptied whole villages.

senses.gloss: The moving of data or software from one system to another.
examples: The *migration* to the new database took all weekend.
IT scheduled the *migration* for a Sunday night.
We lost a few old files during the *migration*.

senses.gloss: The work of a religious minister, or a church program that carries it out.
senses.ru: служение, духовный сан; церковная служба помощи
examples: He left law school and entered the *ministry*.
Their church runs a prison *ministry* downtown.
After thirty years in the *ministry*, she retired last spring.

senses.gloss: A thick venomous snake of the American South that lives near water.
examples: A *moccasin* was sunning itself on the fallen log.
Watch the bank down there — the creek is full of *moccasins*.
He swore the snake in the pond was a *moccasin*, not a harmless water snake.

senses.gloss: The checking of posts on a website and the removal of ones that break its rules.
examples: The company hired hundreds of people for content *moderation*.
*Moderation* on that forum is pretty light.
Weak *moderation* let the comment section turn ugly.

senses.gloss: Someone who checks posts on a website and removes ones that break the rules.
examples: A *moderator* deleted the thread within minutes.
She volunteers as a *moderator* for a parenting group.
The *moderators* banned him for a week.

senses.gloss: The growing strength that a process or campaign builds up as it goes on.
examples: The campaign gained *momentum* after the debate.
We lost all our *momentum* when the funding dried up.
The bill has real *momentum* in the Senate now.

senses.gloss: Sole possession of something that other people also want or claim.
examples: Neither party has a *monopoly* on good ideas.
The church once held a *monopoly* on education here.
He talks as if he had a *monopoly* on suffering.

senses.gloss: A walk taken by an astronaut on the surface of the moon.
examples: The crew's first *moonwalk* lasted almost three hours.
Cameras recorded every step of the *moonwalk*.
NASA cut the second *moonwalk* short because of a suit problem.

senses.gloss: The reason someone has for doing a particular thing.
examples: Detectives never established a *motivation* for the crime.
Her *motivation* for taking the job was the health insurance.
The article questions the senator's *motivations*.

senses.gloss: A very large pile or amount of something.
examples: There's a *mountain* of laundry on the bed.
She came back from vacation to a *mountain* of email.
They ran up *mountains* of debt paying for the treatment.

senses.gloss: A molded plastic guard worn over the teeth in sports.
examples: The boxer spat out his *mouthpiece* between rounds.
No player takes the field without a *mouthpiece*.
He boiled the *mouthpiece* to fit it to his teeth.

senses.gloss: The act of moving, or a change of position.
examples: I caught a *movement* out of the corner of my eye.
The brace limits *movement* in her wrist.
Guards watched every *movement* on the security cameras.

senses.gloss: One of the main sections of a symphony or another long piece of music.
examples: The second *movement* is slow and very quiet.
The symphony has four *movements*.
He fell asleep during the last *movement*.
